ideas.text: Find a SAR dataset with classification labels where the images are NOT chips centred on the object. Train SSL on the big normal scenes (where plain DINO should do worse) and test on the object-centred chips. Compare DINO vs RegionDINO there. Candidates: Sentinel-1 scenes + OpenSARShip chips, FUSAR-Ship; cheap version = chips cut from SARDet boxes (6 classes).

replies.text: Tried the cheap version (S1, chips cut from SARDet boxes, 2026-11-20): null. No SSL already gets 81 % mean per-class accuracy at 1 % labels and every SSL row is within split noise. Six coarse classes plus each class coming from only a few source datasets make the task too easy. If we want chip signal from SARDet: a 0.3 % budget, or train on some source datasets and test on others (removes the style shortcut). The Sentinel-1 + OpenSARShip version (fine-grained ship types, same sensor) is still the better test and is untouched.

Dataset search done (datasets/CANDIDATES.md). SARMAE's pool SAR-1M holds OpenSARShip and FUSAR-Ship, so neither is a clean teacher test, and OpenSARShip at 20 m has 3 to 6 usable classes. Best pick: FAIR-CSAR-V1.0 SL (Gaofen-3 1 m scenes, 22 fine-grained classes, 170k boxes, ResNet detector 39 mAP, not in SAR-1M). Cheap extra: SAR-ACD aircraft chips (6 types, ResNet-50 60 % vs SARMAE 95 %). SDFSD (15 ship types) is not released; SRSDD is too small for a pool.

ideas.text: Framing from the arm-I null result: the object views pay off only when the SSL images are scenes and the test is a chip (cross-dataset +9.4 at 1 %, in-domain -2.0). Claim it as a no-label method for learning from scene archives, not as a better DINO in general. Keep the random-window control in the paper as the ablation that shows the regions matter.

Study 2 (parked until study 1 is analyzed): SSL on blind 2x2 tiles of the SARDet scenes (256 px quarters of the 512-resized scene, no object knowledge, 4x more images, equal optimizer steps = 25 epochs), then the same chip classification. Asks whether smaller SSL images alone close the RegionDINO gap. Design in SARDet_chips/DESIGN.md section 5; needs tiles.csv + an on-the-fly tile loader in the SSL code, regions per tile, about 450 GPU-h of new SSL.

replies.text: S1 came out null (no method separates on SARDet chips), so S2 would compare tile SSL against a flat line. Keep parked unless the chip test is made harder first.

ideas.text: Scale-sweep study: the detection result says crop scale matters, placement does not. Sweep the SSL view size relative to the object size on the SARDet pool (e.g. 48 / 96 / 160 / 224 / whole scene) and map gain vs view-size-to-object-size ratio for detection and for chip transfer. Cheap (same engine, same pool), gives a rule of thumb: match SSL view scale to target scale. A clean finding for the paper.

ideas.text: Attention-proposed regions: replace the brightness rule with regions proposed by a large SAR model (e.g. SARATR-X attention / saliency), still label-free, and keep training only the compact MobileNetV2. Fixes the blob limitation (faint targets, bright clutter) and makes the method object-centric distillation. Compare brightness rule vs attention rule vs random with the same views.

ideas.text: Shadow-consistent SSL: SAR range direction is known per image, so a target and its radar shadow sit at a known offset. Use target-region / shadow-region pairs as a label-free positive pair or prediction task. Uses the one physical fact every amplitude image carries without complex data. Speculative; would need a check that the proposer can find shadows.
